Nonsense. The entire premise behind his argument is that the aggressive rune and piercing rune have costs that are so stupidly low that they can be spammed super easy. You said those spells could've been saved for board control, but bear in mind the entire point of piercing rune is that it hits face WHILE hurting a follower, essentially being a mini-attack that costs 1 point. The aggressive rune is absurd, because evolving him lets you rush something with buffer stats AND gets you a versatile attack card while still leaving you with mana for whatever. For reference, a similar warrior card does a similar job, but costs 4 mana, has one more health and cannot hurt face. Rune's cards help stabilize the board WHILE damaging the opponent, which makes them super difficult to properly manage. Also keep in mind those 1-cost spells will help spellboost ridiculously fast. Imagine an empty board, with the Rune player on Turn 5. He can drop the aggressive rune, evolve him and Rush a follower, play 2 Piercing Runes and kill another 2 (one of which is probably an evolved follower), and drop a high-cost spell on face.
